subject: Clarification: streaming response billing for disconnects and retry behavior
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika@saasify.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming charges for partial responses / retries (logs attached)

Hi Logan,

We ran into an incident yesterday where several streaming responses were cut off mid-generation due to client disconnects. Our engineers saw the model start producing text, then the client TCP connection dropped. The metrics show tokens were billed for those requests and we want to understand Redwood's policy here.

Specific questions:
- Do we get billed for tokens that were generated but never fully delivered to the client (partial segments)?
- If a user retries the same request right after a disconnect, can that trigger double billing, or is there an idempotency/duplication protection?
- Is there a standard crediting process for these types of incidents?

I've attached a short log excerpt (incident-20261012-stream-logs.txt) showing a few example request_ids. We're finalizing a monthly invoice reconciliation and would like clarity so we can correctly attribute charges. If possible, can someone confirm whether this is eligible for a one-off credit while we evaluate using an idempotency token in our client?

Thanks — can we set up a quick 30-minute call if needed.

Best,
Anika Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
SaaSify Inc.

Subject: Re: Streaming charges for partial responses / retries (logs attached)

Hi Anika — thanks for the logs and the clear reproduction steps. Looping in Laura (billing) and Jordan (AE) so we can handle both the technical explanation and any invoice adjustments.

High-level: our hosted metering charges are per-token generated by the model runtime and recorded by our gateway. Practically that means: tokens that our service emits to the network are the ones that show up on the bill. If a connection is severed mid-stream, you are billed for tokens the runtime produced up to the point the server emitted them.

That said, there are two built-in protections I want you to be aware of:
1) Idempotency: if you include an idempotency key (idempotent_request_id) with your request, our gateway will de-duplicate retries for the same request_id for a short window (we'll confirm the exact window below). Retries that present the same idempotency key and the same input should not result in duplicate billed generations.
2) Incident credits: for clear-cut service-related disconnects, we can apply a goodwill credit after verification of logs and request_ids. The credit handling is done through billing — Laura, Marcus, can you propose the credit approach for this account?

If helpful, we can also share the latest RateCard-2026Q4.pdf which explains baseline per-token rates and the discount bands tied to committed volumes. Attaching it now. I'm available for a 30-min sync this week.

— Logan
Product Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Streaming charges for partial responses / retries (logs attached)

Hi Anika — thanks for the patience. I reviewed the logs Logan attached and cross-referenced them with our gateway events. Quick summary and proposal: 

Summary findings:
- The request_ids in your log show the server emitted tokens for 8 requests where the client disconnected mid-stream; the gateway recorded emitted tokens up to the disconnect for billing.
- Two follow-up retries from the same client did not include an idempotency key and were billed as separate generations.

Proposed remediation for the invoice and next steps:
1) Immediate one-off credit: we're prepared to issue a one-off credit equal to 30% of the billed token charges for the verified incident window (12:03–12:47 UTC on 2026-10-12) as a goodwill gesture while you roll out idempotency keys. For your invoice cycle, that will appear as a negative line item on the next invoice unless you'd prefer a direct refund.
2) Idempotency policy: we'll honor deduplication when an idempotent_request_id is present and the payload matches exactly. For hosted API, dedup window is 120 seconds from the first receipt of the request. Retries with the same idempotency key within that window are not charged twice.
3) Long-term: if this account opts into a committed volume (monthly baseline) we can bake in tighter protection and a 0.5% SLA credit threshold for streaming disconnects under our SLA exceptions process. That requires a short amendment to the contract (template attached: SLA-exceptions-template.docx).

Pricing context (refer to attached RateCard): baseline hosted generation rates are listed on the rate card. As a reference example only: at list, generation tokens are $0.00045/token; committed tiers reduce effective unit costs (see page 3). We'll pull exact tier numbers for your usage band and share a tailored rate.

Marcus — please prepare the invoice adjustment for the 30% credit and confirm whether we need a DocuSign amendment for any SLA exception if the customer asks.

Anika — if you confirm you'd like the credit applied to the next invoice, we'll proceed. Separately, Jordan can schedule technical time to help you implement idempotency headers in your client.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Billing Ops, Redwood Inference

Anika — quick follow-up with the confirmations you asked for: 

- Deduplication behavior: the gateway matches the request payload at the byte level when an idempotent_request_id is provided. That means trivial differences (extra whitespace, trailing newlines) can cause a payload mismatch and bypass dedupe. For safety, we recommend hashing the canonicalized payload (trim whitespace, deterministic serialization) on your side and sending that value as the idempotent payload+request_id.
- Credit: Marcus will issue the 30% credit as a negative line on your next invoice. Marcus — please confirm the exact line item and estimated dollar amount so we can close the loop with Anika.
- Committed tiers: Jordan will prepare a tailored committed-volume quote for SaaSify and include the effective unit price changes.

I'll set up a 30-minute technical/ops slot for this Thursday for Jordan + your infra team.

Thanks everyone — closing in on this.

— Logan
